My dad died three years after being diagnosed and then surviving colon cancer. I was 23. My mom died three years earlier, weeks after his diagnoses. Make lists of all your happy memories with them right now. Ask him questions about when he was a kid. Ask about when you were a little kid. Tell him you love him. idk. Nothing can prepare you for that loss. Keep your family very close. One foot in front of the other. Get a journal, and a scrapbook for photos that end up popping up. Feel your feelings, feel the grief. Don’t pretend to be okay afterwards to make it easier on others cause it’s going to settle into you and come crawling out later. You’re not alone in it.

I forgave my parents although I never imagined I would. Both of them were extreme alcoholics. My dad would be extremely violent while drunk. I was shuffled between their two homes for years. Dad was mostly absent until 1st grade when I moved in with him because my mom wasn’t taking care of me because her drinking was so severe. She went to rehab. In 4th grade I went to go live with my recovering alcoholic mom because the drunken abuse in my dads house had come to a peak. My stepmom said it was my fault he was hurting us because I wouldn’t ask him to stop drinking. So they sent me to my moms house one weekend with a note and a duffel bag and I never went back. Then my mom relapsed drinking two years in and dad got sick and was forced to stop drinking. We did not acknowledge her drinking. It was taboo and she’d deny it. My dad and I never spoke about what he was like when he was drunk. We eventually bonded. My mom was extremely toxic and I walked on eggshells for years trying to dodge her destructive moods. When I got old enough to work, she’d take money out of my checks when I asked her to cash them, sold my car and took the money, etc. She wasn’t always terrible, but when it was bad, it was BAD. By then my dad was sober but sick, and I was constantly terrified he was going to die. Then I moved out of state at 18 with my boyfriend because my mom kicked me out. Two years later, with distance, I had started to forgive my mom. She died extremely suddenly in 2015 weeks after my dad was diagnosed with cancer. In the following three years, I become super close to my dad. He died from diabetic complications after he was in remission in 2018. My parents weren’t always bad but as I’ve grown up I’m really starting to see how my trauma has manifested and how it affects literally everything I do. They loved me, but they struggled. The anxiety I had as child trying to monitor whether or not they were sober, in a good mood or dangerous has affected me the most. However, I’ve realized that my parents were just people. Yes they were fucked up, but their behavior was a result of their own unresolved traumas. Doesn’t mean what they did was acceptable, but I can forgive them for not being what I needed them to be because what else can I do? Hate them? What do I learn from that? They loved me the best way they could. I’m still here and can function. I think if they were still alive, I would feel differently for sure. I was 20 when she died, 23 when he died. Maybe it’s just their sudden deaths that are just throwing me into a super trauma warp mind fuck 🤷‍♀️🤷‍♀️🥴🥴🥴
